issues.label: Statutory elements under ORS 609.035
issues.why: Court must identify each element of the offense as it existed at trial and ensure all are met.

issues.label: Which statutory version applies
issues.why: The 2025 amendment postdates conviction, so the court must apply the version in effect at trial.

issues.label: Criminal negligence mental state
issues.why: ORS 161.085(10) may supply the culpable mental state and the court must determine whether it applies and was proven.

issues.label: Whether mens rea was addressed
issues.why: The court's element findings omitted any criminal-negligence determination, raising whether the requisite culpable mental state was found.

issues.label: Location where no right to exclude
issues.why: The offense requires the injury occur where defendant cannot lawfully exclude others; disputed factual finding.

issues.label: Where incident 'began' vs. occurred
issues.why: Court found it 'began' on non-excludable premises but injury may have occurred in defendant's yard, implicating statutory location element.

issues.label: Provocation defense
issues.why: Whether Baby Girl provoked the dogs (biting Zorro) negates an element and is factually disputed.

issues.label: Provocation by another animal
issues.why: Court must decide whether provocation includes a third dog's aggression toward defendant's dog Zorro.

issues.label: Causation of physical injury
issues.why: State must prove defendant's dogs, without provocation, caused the injuries shown in photos.

issues.label: Credibility determinations
issues.why: Court must weigh conflicting eyewitness accounts (Gaul, Shoesmith vs. McCrery) to resolve factual disputes.

issues.label: Sufficiency of physical evidence
issues.why: Photos of fence and knocked-over decorative fence bear on which theory of the break-in is correct.

issues.label: Prior conviction admissibility and use
issues.why: Prior nuisance conviction may be an element or improper propensity evidence requiring limiting consideration.

issues.label: Beyond a reasonable doubt standard
issues.why: Court must apply the correct burden to each disputed element.

issues.label: Two separate counts justification
issues.why: Court must determine whether two dogs and one victim support two distinct counts.

issues.label: Domestic animal status of Baby Girl
issues.why: Statute requires injury to a domestic animal, an element the court must confirm.

issues.label: Validity of pro se and jury waivers
issues.why: Court must ensure defendant knowingly and voluntarily waived counsel and jury trial.

issues.label: Keeper/owner status of defendant
issues.why: Court found this undisputed but must confirm defendant is a statutorily responsible keeper.

issues.label: Whether fence-breaking negates lawful exclusion
issues.why: Court must analyze whether dogs breaching the fence changes the location analysis for excludability.
